text.title: Internationalization Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end trace: a three-locale rollout with RTL, from the audit counts through each gate to the artefact matching the output contract.

section.title: Trace
section.p: Audit of an existing LTR product finds 142 hardcoded English strings, 3 currency values built by string concatenation, and 18 `margin-left` declarations on layout containers. Target locales: `en`, `es`, `ar` — the third forces RTL.

Gates walked in decision-tree order: hardcoded strings > 0 blocks first, so step 2 externalises all 142 behind `t(key)` and adds the lint rule. The 3 concatenations then trip the ICU gate and become plural/currency patterns. The 18 physical properties trip the logical-CSS gate. Pseudo-loc in CI catches four more strings that the codemod missed because they lived in an email template. The key-drift gate fails once — `ar.json` is 31 keys behind after the first translation round — and passes after re-import. The fallback chain is written down as `ar` → `en`, not left to the library.

example.note: `physical_css_props` is 2, not 0: both are direction-fixed elements (a mathematical notation block and a cursor offset), which r4 allows. Zero is not the target — unjustified physical properties are.
